findings.F1: Over the next 3 days, a coin rises more when its last 3 days were unusually volatile against its 30-day volatility (its 18-bar standard deviation of 4h returns over its 180-bar one). The top decile of that ratio was followed by an excess return of +0.242 of the usual 3-day move, which is +2.05 % (t 4.75, 515 non-overlapping cases), about 10 times the 0.19 % cost of a buy and a sell. The other nine deciles lie between -0.108 and +0.041.
findings.F2: The volatility-expansion effect of F1 holds on every coin and in every year but one. The top quintile minus the bottom quintile is positive on all 6 coins (+0.06 on ETH to +0.36 on LTC, in usual moves) and in 7 of 8 years (2025 is flat at +0.027 against +0.026).
findings.F3: The same pattern shows on the bar range. When the last 3 days' mean 4h range is high against its 30-day mean, the excess 3-day return is +0.137 (t 2.87) and +0.128 (t 2.30) in its two top deciles. The bottom decile gives -0.089 (t -1.99), 515 cases each.
findings.F4: A wide recent range helps after both a 3-day rise and a 3-day fall, but more after a rise. After a rise, the top third by recent range gives +0.094 (t 2.45, 901 cases) against -0.013 for the bottom third. After a fall, the top third gives +0.045 (t 1.20) against -0.062 (t -2.02).
findings.F5: Against the brief, the narrowest two-day stretches are followed by underperformance, not by a large move up. The quintile where the 30-day mean 4h range is largest against the 2-day range is followed by -0.101 of the usual move, -0.88 % (t -3.22, 1030 cases). The widest-stretch quintile gives +0.063 (t 1.75).
findings.F6: Upward breaks above the prior 2-day high add nothing on the grid: +0.048 (t 0.83, 385 cases), with no order across narrowness terciles (-0.007, +0.118, +0.004). This matches the inconclusive verdict, whose strength was 0.023.
findings.F7: The other effects I looked at are either below cost or not clear of chance, given about 15 groupings examined.

ideas.idea: The more a coin's 3-day realised volatility exceeds its 30-day realised volatility, the more the coin rises over the next 3 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader leans long a coin whose last three days were far more volatile than its month, and refuses longs in its quietest stretches.
ideas.name: volatility expansion lifts returns

ideas.idea: The narrower a coin's last 2-day price range is compared with its 30-day average 4-hour range, the further its return over the next 3 days falls below its normal drift.
ideas.consequence: A trader refuses long bets placed out of very quiet ranges and treats deep quiet as a reason to stay out.
ideas.name: quiet ranges precede weakness
